reason: E2 directly supports boron's role in improving grain-boundary cohesion and ductility in the same alloy system, but E1 only describes DCT-induced stress states and phase transitions in a general HEA context without evidence for fine grain-boundary precipitation or synergy with boron. The combined synergistic effect and preservation of impact energy release are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Boron doping (0.05–0.1 at.%) improves grain-boundary cohesion and ductility in BCC RHEAs via boride precipitation.
Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) induces beneficial compressive residual stresses and promotes fine grain-boundary phase precipitation.
The combined intervention synergistically improves ductility without degrading strength or impact energy release.
The baseline HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy has limited ductility (~12% fracture strain) and high strength.
